Matumizi ya Lugha katika Tamthiliya ya ( Sadaka ya John Okello ) Awhida
“Art as Technique” na kusema ili mwanafasihi aweze kuwasilisha hisia zake ipasavyo katika fasihi ni lazima hisia hizo azijenge katika hali ya ugeni kwa wasomaji au wasikilizaji kwa kutumia vipengele vya matumizi ya lugha (Schmitz, 2007; Carter, 2006).
Vipengele vya matumizi ya lugha ni kama vile semi, tamathali za semi, taswira, lugha ngeni au za asili zilizo tofauti na kazi yenyewe ya fasihi.
Anaongezea kwa kusema ugeni wa kipindi fulani ni tofauti na ugeni wa kipindi kingine.
Hii ina maana kwamba ugeni katika kazi za fasihi ni lazima ubadilikebadilike kutokana na hadhira, mada, mazingira, na wakati ambapo itaiepusha kazi ya fasihi kuwa ya kimazoea na badala yake kuipa uhai upya kila iitwapo leo.
Shklovisky anasisitiza dhana ya ugeni kwa kusema sio ya kubadilisha maana bali ni ya jinsi au namna ya kuelezea jambo.
Utangulizi Matumizi ya lugha ni kipengele kimojawapo katika umbo la nje la kazi ya fasihi, yaani fani.
Fani hujumbuisha viungo msingi vyote vinavyotumika kuumba kazi ya fasihi kwa mfano mandhari, wahusika, muundo, mtindo, jina la kazi/diwani n.k.
Katika kipengele cha matumizi ya lugha wahakiki hutazama vipengele hivi; semi, tamathali za semi, rejesta, lugha za kigeni n.k kutegemea na lengo la mhakiki.
Katika makala haya tunatalii matumizi ya lugha katika tamthiliya ya Sadaka ya John Okello (2015).
Tamthiliya hii imeandikwa na Emmanuel Mbogo, mwanafasihi kutoka nchini Tanzania.
Ni tamthiliya inayozungumzia mapinduzi ya Serikali ya Zanzibar, yaliyofanyika mwaka 1964.
Nadharia ya Umaumbo ndiyo itakayoongoza mjadala wetu.
Nadharia hii imeegema zaidi kwenye kuchambua matumizi ya lugha katika kazi za fasihi.
Washadidi wa nadharia hii wanaona kwamba kila kazi ya kifasihi inatumia nadharia hii kwani inahusika na kipengele msingi katika tawi hili la sanaa, fasihi nguzo msingi yake ni lugha.
Katika tamthiliya hii tutabainisha vipengele mbalimbali vya matumizi ya lugha huku tukiongozwa na nadharia ya umaumbo.
1.1 Nadharia ya Umaumbo
Schmitz (2007) na Carter (2006) wameainisha mawazo kadha wa kadha ya wananadharia wa umaumbo kama ifuatavyo; Kutofautisha matumizi ya lugha ya kawaida na lugha ya kifasihi, waliamini na kusisitiza kwamba dhana ya ugeni au upya ndiyo dhima kuu ya sanaa na walipenda uhakiki wa fasihi uwe na mwelekeo wa kisayansi na hivyo walitaka kuanzisha usayansi katika fasihi
Kwa mujibu wa mawazo ya wanamaumbo, kazi zote za fasihi hutumia nadharia hii kwa sababu kazi ya fasihi haiwezi kuwa ya kifasihi kama haitakuwa na usanaa ndani yake.
Sanaa hizo ni ujenzi wa vipengele vya lugha vinavyoonesha upya wa kazi hiyo.
Hivyo basi mtu yeyote atakayehakiki kazi yoyote ya fasihi kwa kuzingatia nadharia ya umaumbo ni wazi swala la “upya” yaani vipengele vijengavyo matumizi ya lugha haviwezi kuepukika.
Nadharia ya umaumbo ni miongoni mwa nadharia zinazohakiki na kufafanua matumizi ya lugha katika taaluma ya fasihi na isimu.
Nadharia hii ilitokana na wanaharakati wa pande mbili za kisomi huko Urusi: upande wa kwanza ni ule wa wanaisimu wa Moscow (Moscow Linguistics Circle) na upande wa pili ni ule wa chama cha uhakiki wa lugha ya Kishairi (Society for the Study of Poetic Language-OPAYAZ) wote wakiwa na lengo la kuleta mapinduzi kwenye isimu na uhakiki wa fasihi (Schmitz, 2007).
Kwa kuhitimisha nadharia ya umaumbo imechangia kwa kiasi kikubwa harakati za ukuzaji na maendeleo ya uhakiki wa fasihi.
Mchango huo umetokana na dhana ya ugeni au upya katika kazi za fasihi, changamoto na mijadala mbalimbali iliyoibua maarifa na mawazo mbalimbali katika taaluma ya fasihi na uanzishaji wa nadharia nyingine kama ile ya nadharia ya usasa.
1.2 Matumizi ya Lugha katika Tamthiliya ya Sadaka ya John Okello
1.2.1 Tashbiha
Hii ni tamathali ya semi inayounganisha vitu viwili au zaidi vyenye mshabaha.
Maneno yanayotumiwa zaidi katika tamathali hii ni haya; kama, mithili ya, mfano wa, kama vile, n.k Katika tamthiliya yetu teule tamathali hii imejitokeza pahala pengi.
Mtunzi wetu Emmanuel Mbogo amejitahidi kuitumia kila onyesho kadri ya masemezano ya wahusika wake.
Tashbiha zilizojitokeza ni hizi zifuatazo:
“…Uhuru wa Zanzibar unanukia kama marashi ya Pemba…” (uk.1)
Wengi wa wanaharakati hawa walikuwa vijana waliojuana na kufahamiana kwani waliweza kujadiliana kwa pamoja huku wakikubaliana na kupingana kwa baadhi ya maarifa.
Walikuwa na hamasa na mwamko wa kuanzisha maarifa ya kitaaluma kwa namna yoyote ile ikiwemo kwa njia ya mijadala.
Katika mijadala yao walijitambulisha kama wanaurasimu (formalistics) wenye lengo la kuleta mapinduzi katika taaluma.
Pia waliweza kufanya maandamano kwenye miji ya St.Peterburg na Moscow kabla ya mapinduzi ya mwaka 1917.
Kutokana na juhudi za wanaharakati hawa waliweza kufunua mambo mbalimbali ya kitamaduni yaliyoko Urusi kama vile muziki, sanaa, fasihi na isimu.
Kipindi cha machafuko na vita vya wenyewe kwa wenyewe wanaurasimu walipiga hatua za kudai haki zao lakini walizuiliwa na wanaukomunisti kwa kudai kwamba wanaenda kinyume na itikadi za uhalisia wa kijamaa.
Walijitahidi kueleza itikadi zao lakini hawakufanikiwa na mwaka 1930 ikawa ndiyo usambalatisho wa kikundi cha wanaurasimu huko Urusi.
Pamoja na msambalatisho huo mawazo yao yaliendelezwa na baadhi ya wanaurasimu kama Victor Shklovsky, Roman Jakobson na wengineo katika uwanja wa taaluma ya fasihi kwa wanataaluma wengine nje ya Urusi.

Wanamaumbo waliibua dhana kuu mbili katika fasihi: dhana ya kwanza ni ile ya uzoeaji (habitualization) na dhana ya pili ni ya ugeni (defamiliarisation).
Kwa mujibu wa Carter (2006) anaona kwamba dhana ya uzoeaji inajitokeza pale jambo linapotumika mara kwa mara hadi kufikia hali ya kujiendesha lenyewe (automatically).

1.2.5 Takriri/Shada
Kisiwani Unguja.
Pia katika uk.
4 mtunzi amemfananisha Sultan Jamshid na vitu mbalimbali kama vile nahodha, rubani na jemedari.
Neno kama limetumika kufanya ulinganisho huu katika tamthiliya hii ya Sadaka ya John Okello.
1.2.2 Tashihisi
Haya ni maneno yanayotolewa kusisitiza au kutilia mkazo jambo fulani.
Mbinu hii inajitokeza zaidi katika utanzu wa ushairi ingawa katika tanzu nyingine hujitokeza pia (Mulokozi 1999).
Takriri inaweza kujitokeza kwa kurudiwa rudiwa neno au mizani au mkarara au kina.
Katika tamthiliya teule, Sadaka ya John Okello tamthali hii imetumika.
Mtunzi ametumia takriri hizi;
ASHURA: “Leo!
Leo!” Leo saa ngapi… (uk.14)
Hii ni tamathali inayotumika kwa kuvipa viumbe sifa za kutenda kama binadamu, kwamba kitu kisicho na uhai kupewa uwezo wa kufanya kama mwanadamu afanyavyo.
Katika ukurasa wa sita ndani ya tamthiliya teule, Mhusika RASHID ametumika kuonyesha tamathali hii ya tashihisi.
Rashid anasema,
“Ati sina mama, mbuyu ulipasuka, nikazaliwa?” (Uk.6)
Takriri imejitokeza kama neno ‘leo’ katika tamko hilo la mhusika Ashura.
Mhusika huyu ametumika neno hili kuonyesha msisitizo.
Anataka mwenzake abainishe waziwazi hilo analolisema atalikamilisha leo saa ngapi?
Maana siku ya leo ina masaa mengi.
1.2.6 Semi
Mbuyu ni mmea.
Jinsi mimea inavyozaana ni tofauti na binadamu anavyozaliwa.
Kwenye tamko hili la RASHID mmea huu umepewa sifa ya kuzaa kama binadamu.
Tashihisi hii imetumika kuibua tafakuri kwa wakoloni waliokuwa wakiwatesa wakazi wa Zanzibar, kwamba wawaheshimu hawa watu weusi pia ambao wamezaliwa kama binadamu wengine.
Mulokozi (1996) anasema semi ni kauli fupi zilizobeba maana nzito ndani yake.
Katika fasihi simulizi ya Kiswahili inadaiwa kuwa semi ni tokeo la idili ndefu za kimaisha walizopitia wahenga, ndiyo maana mara nyingi zinaonekana kuwa kweli kila zinapotolewa.
Katika utanzu huu kuna vipera mbalimbali mathalani, methali, vitendawili, nahau na misemo.
Methali zimetumika katika tamthiliya hii teule.
Aina hii ya semi huwa na pande mbili, upande wa kwanza hueleza jambo na upande wa pili hueleza tokeo lake.
Emmanuel Mbogo ametumia methali hizi;
Vilevile katika uk.3 mtunzi anasema, “Historia iliyofumbata ua la Alizeti au ua la Waridi.” Uwezo wa kushika kitu na kufumbata anao binadamu.
Binadamu hufumbata kitu kupitia mikono yake.
Katika kauli hii mtunzi anaipa historia uwezo wa kibinadamu, kwamba hushikilia, hutunza na kuhifadhi mambo mazuri zaidi.
Maua ya Alzeti na Waridi yametumika kuakisi mambo mema, mazuri yanayovutia katika jamii.

OKELLO: Chenye mwanzo, kina mwisho (uk.17)
RASHIDI:…Ni dua tu la kuku lisilomtisha mwewe…(uk.17)
Katika tamathali hii maneno yanayotolewa huwa na maana tofauti kabisa na maana lengwa.
Inamhitaji hadhira kuwaza kwa kina ili kung’amua maana inayorejelewa.
Mtunzi ametumia tamathali hii pia katika tamthiliya hii teule.

Mvumilivu, hula mbovu (uk.68)
Watu hawa watatu wanaosemwa humo na mhusika Okello kasi yao ya utendaji imeshushwa mno.
Imepunguzwa mno hata kufikia kulinganishwa na mwendo wa kobe ambao wajulikana kuwa taratibu mno, kwa lugha isiyoweza kutamkika.
Hakika hii ni kejeli au kinaya kwa walengwa katika kauli hii.
Wanakumbushwa kufanya mambo kwa wepesi zaidi.
1.2.4 Dhihaka
Hii ni tamathali yenye ubeuzi mkali sana (Senkoro 1981).
Maneno yanayosikika ni tofauti na maana lengwa kabisa.
Mhusika mmoja, BIBI ametumiwa na mtunzi kuwakilisha tamathali hii ndani ya tamthiliya teule.
BIBI: …Mungu mnayemwabudu amekuwa mjomba wenu?...
(uk.64)
Methali hii ya Umoja ni nguvu na utengano ni udhaifu hutumika kuhamasisha umoja miongoni mwa wanajumuiya.
Huweka msisitizo watu kushikamana pamoja katika jambo lolote wanaloliendea.
Methali hii ameitumia mtunzi kupitia muhusika waje Okello alipokuwa akiwahamasisha vijana wenzake kuingia vitani ili kufanya mapinduzi na hatmaye kujipatia uhuru wa kweli katika ardhi yao.
Methali mbili za mwisho; Shukrani ya punda, mateke na mvumilivu hula mbovu ni tokeo la majuto anayopitia mhusika wa tamthiliya hii teule, John Okello.
Mhusika mkuu huyu amechangia pakubwa katika ukombozi wa nchi mbalimbali hapa Afrika (Zanzibar ikiwepo) lakini hakukumbukwa pahala popote.
Kila alipokamilisha ukombozi alifukuzwa na kuishia gerezani.
Mtunzi ametumbia mbinu ya udenguzi, kusema methali kwa kinyume badala ya kusema mvumilivu hula mbivu akaandika, mvumilivu hula mbovu.
Hii yote ilikuwa kuonesha sikitiko la mhusika huyu Okello.
1.2.7 Misemo
Mhusika BIBI anauliza swali kwa watu wanaoonekana kumwabudu Mungu kila uchao huku matendo yao yamejaa dhuluma na uonevu mkali.
Matendo wanayoyafanya haya akisi mafunzo ya Mwenyezi Mungu.
Wanatesa watu, watumwa na wengine wote wanaokatiza mbele ya macho yao wasio na rangi kama yao.
Swali hili hakika ni dhihaka kwa hao wanaoonekana kumcha Mungu huku wakitenda maovu.
Mtunzi anasema, Mola hachezewi, hadanganywi, hafanyiwi
Hizi ni kauli fupifupi ambazo hutumiwa na jamii kusisitiza ukweli wa jambo fulani.
Inasemwa kwamba kauli hizi huunganisha dhana au mawazo tofauti kuwa jambo moja kwa lengo la kufikisha ujumbe uliodhamiriwa.
Ndani ya tamthiliya teule, Sadaka ya John Okello mtunzi ametumia misemo mbalimbali.

This article explores the linguistic uses in the play (John Okello’s Sacrifice). The linguistic elements encompass all the fundamental contents used in literary works. The use of language is considered one of the artistic aspects of a literary work, and art contains all the essential components employed to create a literary piece, such as themes, characters, structure, style, and title. In the aspect of language use, critics examine these features—expressions, metaphors, foreign languages, and so on—depending on the critic's objective. In this article, we explore the use of language in the drama Sacrifice by director John Okello (2015). The play was written by the Tanzanian author Emmanuel Mbujo. It is a play about the revolution of the Zanzibar government that took place in 1964. Here, the researcher relied on analyzing the use of language in this literary work. Literature is a branch of art that uses spoken language or text to convey a message to society. In order for the intended message to reach the community, it is important for authors to use language creatively in conveying the message to the audience. Emmanuel Mbogo, who resides in mainland Tanzania, presents a drama about the people of Zanzibar (Unguja and Pemba). The expressions given to all the characters in this work correspond to the large percentage of the islands’ population. A language is assigned to each character to suit their role. All the elements used may have carried different intentions, but unfortunately the researcher did not utilize them. The elements of language used aimed to conceptualize the various themes in this drama. Certainly, the foundations of structuralist theory have been considered regarding the use of language in the literary work of this drama.

“Art as Technique” states that for a writer to effectively convey their emotions in literature, it is necessary for those emotions to be constructed in a way that presents novelty to the readers or listeners by utilizing elements of language use (Schmitz, 2007; Carter, 2006). Elements of language use include sayings, figures of speech, imagery, and the use of foreign or indigenous languages that are distinct from the literary work itself. He adds by saying that the innovation of one period is different from the innovation of another period. This means that innovation in literary works must constantly change depending on the audience, subject, context, and time, which prevents the literary work from becoming routine and instead gives it renewed vitality each time it is engaged. Shklovisky emphasizes the concept of innovation by stating that it is not about changing the meaning but rather about the manner or way of expressing something. Introduction  
The use of language is one of the aspects found in the external structure of a literary work, that is, its form. Form encompasses all the essential elements used to shape a literary work, such as setting, characters, structure, style, and the title of the work/anthology, among others. In examining the use of language, critics focus on these elements: expressions, figures of speech, register, foreign languages, etc., depending on the critic’s objective. In this article, we explore the use of language in the play *John Okello’s Sacrifice* (2015). This play was written by Emmanuel Mbogo, a literary writer from Tanzania. It is a play that discusses the Zanzibar Revolution, which took place in 1964. The theory of Formalism will guide our discussion. This theory is primarily focused on analyzing the use of language in literary works. Proponents of this theory believe that every literary work employs this approach, as it deals with a fundamental aspect of this branch of art—language, which is the main pillar of literature. In this play, we will identify various elements of language use, guided by the theory of Formalism. 1.1 The Theory of Formalism  
Schmitz (2007) and Carter (2006) have outlined several ideas of formalist theorists as follows: distinguishing between the use of ordinary language and literary language, they believed and emphasized that the concept of innovation or novelty is the main function of art, and they preferred literary criticism to have a scientific orientation; thus, they sought to establish scientific approaches in literature.  
According to the ideas of the formalists, all literary works utilize this theory because a work cannot be considered literary if it does not possess artistic qualities. These artistic qualities involve the construction of language elements that demonstrate the novelty of the work. Therefore, anyone who critiques any literary work based on the theory of Formalism will inevitably have to confront the issue of "novelty"—that is, the features that construct the use of language are unavoidable. The theory of Formalism is among the theories that analyze and explain the use of language in the disciplines of literature and linguistics. This theory originated from activists in two academic circles in Russia: on the one hand, the linguists of the Moscow Linguistics Circle, and on the other, the Society for the Study of Poetic Language (OPAYAZ), both aiming to bring revolutions to linguistics and literary criticism (Schmitz, 2007). In conclusion, the theory of Formalism has greatly contributed to the advancement and development of literary criticism. This contribution stems from the concept of innovation or novelty in literary works, the challenges and various debates it has sparked, which have generated diverse knowledge and ideas within the field of literature, as well as the emergence of other theories such as the theory of Modernism. 1.2 The Use of Language in the Play “John Okello’s Sacrifice”  
1.2.1 Simile  
This is a figure of speech that connects two or more things that share a resemblance. The words most commonly used in this figure of speech include: like, as, similar to, such as, among others. In our selected play, this figure of speech appears in many places. Our author Emmanuel Mbogo has made an effort to use every scene according to the dialogues of his characters. The following similes appear:

These are words used to emphasize or stress a particular issue. This technique is most evident in the genre of poetry, although it also appears in other genres (Mulokozi 1999). Repetition can appear through the recurrence of a word, rhythm, refrain, or rhyme. In the selected play, John Okello's Sacrifice, this figure of speech has been used. The author has used the following repetitions;
ASHURA: “Today! “Today!” Today at what time… (p.14)
This is a figure of speech used to attribute human actions to non-human entities, giving an inanimate thing the ability to act as a human does. On page six of the selected play, the character RASHID is used to illustrate this figure of personification. Rashid says,
“Is it that I have no mother, that the baobab tree split, and I was born?” (p.6)
Repetition appears in the use of the word ‘today’ in the statement by the character Ashura. This character uses the word to convey emphasis. He wants his companion to specify exactly at what time today he will finish what he is talking about, since today has many hours. 1.2.6 Semantics  
The baobab is a plant. The way plants reproduce is different from how human beings are born. In this statement by RASHID, this plant is given the attribute of giving birth like a human being. This personification has been used to provoke reflection among the colonizers who were oppressing the inhabitants of Zanzibar, urging them to also respect these Black people who were born like other human beings. Mulokozi (1996) states that sayings are short expressions that carry deep meaning within them. In Swahili oral literature, it is claimed that sayings are the result of long life experiences that the elders went through, which is why they often appear to be true whenever they are quoted. In this genre, there are various subgenres such as proverbs, riddles, idioms, and sayings. Proverbs have been used in this selected play. It emphasizes that people should stick together in whatever they set out to do. The author uses this proverb through the character Okello as he encourages his fellow youths to go to war in order to stage a revolution and ultimately attain true freedom in their land. The last two proverbs, "A donkey’s gratitude is a kick" and "Patience ends up eating what is spoiled," reflect the regret experienced by the main character of this play, John Okello. This main character made a significant contribution to the liberation of various countries in Africa (including Zanzibar), but was not remembered anywhere. Every time he completed a liberation struggle, he was expelled and ended up in prison. The author has used the technique of irony, stating the proverb in reverse; instead of saying “Patience ends up eating what is ripe,” he wrote “Patience ends up eating what is spoiled.” All this was to express the sorrow of this character, Okello. 1.2.7 Idioms

The Use of Language in the Play (John Okello’s Sacrifice) Awhida

“Art as Technique” states that for a writer to effectively convey their emotions in literature, it is necessary for those emotions to be constructed in a way that presents novelty to the readers or listeners by utilizing elements of language use (Schmitz, 2007; Carter, 2006). Elements of language use include sayings, figures of speech, imagery, and the use of foreign or indigenous languages that are distinct from the literary work itself.

Introduction  
The use of language is one of the aspects found in the external structure of a literary work, that is, its form. Form encompasses all the essential elements used to shape a literary work, such as setting, characters, structure, style, and the title of the work/anthology, among others. In examining the use of language, critics focus on these elements: expressions, figures of speech, register, foreign languages, etc., depending on the critic’s objective. In this article, we explore the use of language in the play *John Okello’s Sacrifice* (2015).

1.1 Nadharia ya Umaumbo
Schmitz (2007) na Carter (2006) wameainisha mawazo kadha wa kadha ya wananadharia wa umaumbo kama ifuatavyo; Kutofautisha matumizi ya lugha ya kawaida na lugha ya kifasihi, waliamini na kusisitiza kwamba dhana ya ugeni au upya ndiyo dhima kuu ya sanaa na walipenda uhakiki wa fasihi uwe na mwelekeo wa kisayansi na hivyo walitaka kuanzisha usayansi katika fasihi
Kwa mujibu wa mawazo ya wanamaumbo, kazi zote za fasihi hutumia nadharia hii kwa sababu kazi ya fasihi haiwezi kuwa ya kifasihi kama haitakuwa na usanaa ndani yake. Sanaa hizo ni ujenzi wa vipengele vya lugha vinavyoonesha upya wa kazi hiyo. Hivyo basi mtu yeyote atakayehakiki kazi yoyote ya fasihi kwa kuzingatia nadharia ya umaumbo ni wazi swala la “upya” yaani vipengele vijengavyo matumizi ya lugha haviwezi kuepukika. Nadharia ya umaumbo ni miongoni mwa nadharia zinazohakiki na kufafanua matumizi ya lugha katika taaluma ya fasihi na isimu. Nadharia hii ilitokana na wanaharakati wa pande mbili za kisomi huko Urusi: upande wa kwanza ni ule wa wanaisimu wa Moscow (Moscow Linguistics Circle) na upande wa pili ni ule wa chama cha uhakiki wa lugha ya Kishairi (Society for the Study of Poetic Language-OPAYAZ) wote wakiwa na lengo la kuleta mapinduzi kwenye isimu na uhakiki wa fasihi (Schmitz, 2007).
discourses.translated_txt:
1.1 The Theory of Formalism  
Schmitz (2007) and Carter (2006) have outlined several ideas of formalist theorists as follows: distinguishing between the use of ordinary language and literary language, they believed and emphasized that the concept of innovation or novelty is the main function of art, and they preferred literary criticism to have a scientific orientation; thus, they sought to establish scientific approaches in literature.  
According to the ideas of the formalists, all literary works utilize this theory because a work cannot be considered literary if it does not possess artistic qualities. These artistic qualities involve the construction of language elements that demonstrate the novelty of the work. Therefore, anyone who critiques any literary work based on the theory of Formalism will inevitably have to confront the issue of "novelty"—that is, the features that construct the use of language are unavoidable. The theory of Formalism is among the theories that analyze and explain the use of language in the disciplines of literature and linguistics. This theory originated from activists in two academic circles in Russia: on the one hand, the linguists of the Moscow Linguistics Circle, and on the other, the Society for the Study of Poetic Language (OPAYAZ), both aiming to bring revolutions to linguistics and literary criticism (Schmitz, 2007).

discourses.source_txt: Kwa kuhitimisha nadharia ya umaumbo imechangia kwa kiasi kikubwa harakati za ukuzaji na maendeleo ya uhakiki wa fasihi. Mchango huo umetokana na dhana ya ugeni au upya katika kazi za fasihi, changamoto na mijadala mbalimbali iliyoibua maarifa na mawazo mbalimbali katika taaluma ya fasihi na uanzishaji wa nadharia nyingine kama ile ya nadharia ya usasa.
discourses.translated_txt: In conclusion, the theory of Formalism has greatly contributed to the advancement and development of literary criticism. This contribution stems from the concept of innovation or novelty in literary works, the challenges and various debates it has sparked, which have generated diverse knowledge and ideas within the field of literature, as well as the emergence of other theories such as the theory of Modernism.

1.3 Comments and Recommendations  
Our author, Emmanuel Mbogo, has made excellent use of language in the construction of this play. From the beginning to the end, the reader is continually engaged with this work. The innovation described by structuralists in theory truly manifests itself in this work.

1.4 Hitimisho
Fasihi ni tawi la sanaa linalotumia lugha ya mazungumzo au maandishi kufikisha ujumbe kwa jamii. Ili ujumbe lengwa uweze kufika kwa jamii ni vema watunzi wakatumia lugha kiubunifu katika kuifikishia hadhira ujumbe huo.
discourses.translated_txt:
1.4 Conclusion  
Literature is a branch of art that uses spoken or written language to convey a message to society. For the intended message to reach the community effectively, it is important for writers to use language creatively in delivering that message to the audience.

discourses.source_txt: Emmanuel Mbogo ni mkazi wa Tanzania bara, tamthiliya aliyoitunga inahusu watu wa Zanzibar (Unguja na Pemba). Matamshi waliyopewa wahusika wote katika kazi hii yanaendana na wakazi wa visiwani asilimia kubwa. Alipoongea mwarabu, lugha imemtambulisha. Alipoongea mzawa wa Unguja, lugha imemtambulisha, alipoongea mtumwa kutoka bara, kwenye msafara wa watumwa kutoka Tabora naye lugha imemtambulisha.
discourses.translated_txt: Emmanuel Mbogo is a resident of mainland Tanzania, and the play he wrote concerns the people of Zanzibar (Unguja and Pemba). The accents given to all the characters in this work largely match those of the island inhabitants. When an Arab character speaks, the language identifies him. When a native of Unguja speaks, the language identifies him as well. When a slave from the mainland, part of a caravan of slaves from Tabora, speaks, the language also identifies him.

discourses.source_txt: Wahusika wote wamepewa lugha kuendana na uhusika wao.
